entries.title: Trump effectively ended asylum. Advocates look to the Supreme Court to restore it

entries.snippet: The announcement opened the latest chapter in an ongoing struggle between the U.S. and Mexican governments over who has the right to take action against cartels in Mexico.

entries.snippet: The 2019 law, known as Bill 21, bans religious symbols — including Muslim headscarves, Sikh turbans, Jewish skullcaps and Christian crosses — for workers covered by it.

entries.snippet: A military aircraft fired "precision munitions" at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer on Thursday, and the "ship's propulsion was ultimately disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed," U.S. Central Command said in a statement.

entries.snippet: In their search for their dwindling food source, the whales are spending less time in the Salish Sea, the maze of inland waters between Washington State and British Columbia.

entries.snippet: The spending package is small compared to national budgets — around 1% to 1.2% of gross national income — but it encapsulates the ambitions of the world's biggest trading bloc and how it sees itself on the international stage.

entries.title: Los Angeles schools block Google's AI features, consider dropping tech giant's products
entries.snippet: The LA district, which enrolls half a million students, has made no formal announcement, and the move caught parents and students by surprise, said Bridie Lee, a leader of Schools Beyond Screens LA.

entries.title: Serbia's student movement proposes a chemistry professor for presidency ahead of Dec. 27 ballot
entries.snippet: The presidential vote comes after the student movement defeated former President Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early parliamentary ballot on Oct. 25.

entries.title: Zelenskyy urges the U.S. to pressure Putin, calling Trump's 'my friend' remark strange
entries.snippet: "He can't be a friend," Zelenskyy told the BBC in Kyiv, likening it to someone calling Adolf Hitler a friend during World War II.

entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill
entries.snippet: Quebec's government passed Bill 21 to ban religious symbols for public servants, arguing it was necessary to protect its secularist society. Critics argue the bill weakens legal protections for fundamental rights.

entries.title: Germany news: Lawmakers approve debt-laden 2027 budget
entries.snippet: German lawmakers voted on a federal budget which foresees €556 billion in spending. Elsewhere, the Left Party is hosting a summit on femicide and the BSW party conference starts in Dresden. DW has more.

entries.title: Spanish rider Marc Marquez announces MotoGP retirement, days after clinching record 8th world title
entries.snippet: Marc Marquez took fans and his team by surprise when announcing this weekend's race in Valencia will be his last. The 33-year-old won a record eight MotoGP titles, including his rookie and retirement seasons.

entries.title: France seeks German man in Channel migrant boat probe
entries.snippet: A German businessman is accused of supplying equipment to smugglers organizing migrant crossings from France to the United Kingdom. However, he can't face formal charges until he is extradited to France.

entries.title: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit
entries.snippet: An EU leaders summit on the bloc's seven-year budget fell apart amid divisions over how to fund Ukraine. The budget proposal also includes a 3% tax on US tech companies, in a bid for the EU to generate additional funds.

entries.title: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, Brussels' most anticipated new art museum, opens its doors
entries.snippet: A major addition to Europe's cultural scene: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, the new contemporary art museum in a former Citroen factory complex, is celebrating its opening with a free, nonstop weekend program.

entries.title: Serbia's Student List runs chemistry professor Radomir Saicic for president
entries.snippet: After ousting strongman Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's student movement has now nominated academic Radomir Saicic for the upcoming presidential vote. Saicic accused the "outgoing regime" of trying to collapse the state.

entries.title: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong
entries.snippet: The tiny Vallarta mud turtle was only discovered in 2018. It's critically endangered with around 300 thought to live in the wild. Almost one tenth of that number were stashed in a traveler's luggage, bound in duct tape.

entries.title: Arsenic in the water: Thailand presses Myanmar over mining pollution
entries.snippet: Thailand is seeking to tackle river pollution stemming from rare earth mines in neighboring Myanmar. The two countries held joint talks this week as a "first step towards agreeing on the evidence."

entries.title: Georgia: Police clash with Besiktas fans at Israel club game
entries.snippet: Turkey's Besiktas accused Georgian police of using "disproportionate" force during the game with Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva, which saw Besiktas fans unfurl a banner supporting Palestine.

entries.title: Airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, succumbing to aviation fuel costs
entries.snippet: The low-cost airline was only founded a few years ago and had been struggling to turn a profit. The spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran has now driven Norway's Norse Atlantic into bankruptcy.

entries.title: As Gambia gears up for election, can Barrow secure a third term?
entries.snippet: President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term as Gambians vote on December 5. The election will test the opposition's appeal and the country's progress on democratic reform.

entries.title: Informer TV owner Vucicevic arrested: Has the reckoning with Serbia's pro-Vucic media machine begun?
entries.snippet: The arrest of media owner Dragan J. Vucicevic raises questions about whether Serbia is holding the people behind the country's pro-Vucic media accountable — or whether this is another political power struggle.

entries.title: Duterte's ICC trial: What is at stake for the Philippines?
entries.snippet: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte faces trial in The Hague over his deadly war on drugs. The proceedings could determine the political fortunes of a powerful dynasty. Victims' families hope to see justice.

entries.title: In Iran, child marriage risks complicated by war
entries.snippet: War, poverty and disrupted schooling could put more girls in Iran at risk of child marriage, rights advocates have warned.

entries.title: Philippines: VP Duterte says father's ICC case 'not a fair trial'
entries.snippet: Sara Duterte has said the ICC will not give her father a fair trial and that the Hague-based court wants to "make a statement." Duterte alleges the case against her father is politically motivated.

entries.title: The tiny BSW is a party in crisis, as it is set to hand the far-right AfD power in eastern Germany
entries.snippet: Sahra Wagenknecht's BSW party is set to disrupt German politics yet again. Espousing a mix of left-wing economic policy and populist far-right anti-migration rhetoric, it now stands to play kingmaker to the far right AfD

entries.title: Russia sports ban: Ukraine's Heraskevych hails EU pushback
entries.snippet: As European countries challenge Russia's sporting return, Ukrainian Olympian Vladyslav Heraskevych believes the IOC is facing a "very big crisis."

entries.title: How East Germany boosted Vietnam's coffee industry
entries.snippet: When East Germany could no longer afford to import coffee, it introduced a substitute blend containing rye and chicory in 1977. A public outcry ensued. The solution to the problem lay 9,000 kilometers away — in Vietnam.
